title: Read and select Platter production materials and templates
summary: Understand retained packet artifacts, fixed template boundaries, imports, daily PDF configuration, and explicit private exports.
use_when: A reader needs artifact or template meaning, fixed versus editable content, immutable selection, daily PDF settings, or export behavior.
do_not_use_when: The goal is authoring, sending, source-library mutation, or direct SQLite integration.
outcome: Retained materials and future template/PDF selection are understood through Platter-owned identities and interfaces.
effects: Initialization retains immutable template bytes. Imports atomically select a new immutable template for future captures. Prior runs and editions keep their exact references.

Configuration validates and sets or clears the daily PDF path under normal mutation admission. Export writes a new private destination and refuses overwrite. These interfaces prepare no packets and send nothing.
authority: Platter owns captured inputs, accepted artifacts, selected templates, settings, and export effects. Annals, Weaver, and Nucleus retain their separate source/execution authority.
success: A supported immutable artifact or validated future selection is retained; export writes the selected retained bytes to a new destination.
failure_and_recovery: Invalid templates, overlapping regions, invalid or unreadable configured PDFs, unsupported state, and foreign holds stop the operation. Existing artifacts and frozen editions remain intact.
Use supported maintained migration. Do not query or edit private SQLite as an integration route.
privacy: Template, career, posting, resume, brief, and edition bytes remain private. Nucleus/model, employer HTTP, and authorized Email disclosures follow their separate feature contracts.
does_not_authorize: Model work, an email, recurring activation, or alteration of a captured run or frozen edition.

consumers.statement: The current user and local agents use Platter CLI interfaces to select future templates or daily PDF settings, inspect local state, and export retained artifacts.

preconditions.statement: Use the canonical schema-eight library at ~/.local/share/platter or its sole existing ~/.local/share/job-packets predecessor. Two roots are ambiguous and refused; --state-dir must equal the canonical root. Imports require initialized state and supported separate Jackson/Projects regions and both project marker pairs.

inputs.statement: Initialization and imports accept an absolute private LaTeX source path. PDF configuration accepts an absolute readable valid unencrypted PDF with at least one page. Export accepts an artifact ID and a new explicit destination.

outputs.statement: Artifacts retain immutable bytes, producing-run reference when applicable, kind, filename, media type, and integrity hash. Configuration and selected template references remain in the canonical library; an export is a separate private file.

Retained historical complete-project payloads preserve one or two unique Cell/Wrought entries with description, optional dates, one through eight bullets and private source notes; retained text fields have at most 1000 characters and no controls. Historical rendering supplies fixed project links and omits source notes. Current authoring writes only the fields described by platter.preparation.

data_semantics.statement: A packet is a run and its artifacts. Imported templates and shared daily PDFs have no producing run. Artifact IDs are identities, not file paths; exported copies never become dependencies.

Current tailored templates keep fixed presentation outside Jackson bullets and the two marked project bullet lists. Projects-only imports change only the existing Projects section. Daily override configuration affects future daily work; frozen bytes remain unchanged.

identity_and_units.statement: Run IDs identify preparations; artifact IDs identify retained bytes and kinds. The original template path records provenance rather than a continuing byte source. A daily override path selects an external future-work source; frozen PDF bytes have their own artifact identity.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The schema-eight SQLite library contains retained inputs, templates, artifacts, editions, settings, holds and frozen daily PDF bytes. Current configuration does not refresh sources or establish current posting availability.

access.statement: Use current-user CLI interfaces. Private sources and exports remain outside the repository. No independent live library may bypass canonical mutation admission.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Template selection is atomic and preserves earlier artifacts and captured references. Accepted outputs are immutable by run and kind; repeated identical submission resolves to retained content and conflicting content is refused. Configuration changes affect future work.

operational_limits.statement: Generated template and imported region constraints apply to new tailored work. PDF override validation does not compile LaTeX or impose the tailored one-page/content checks. Export never overwrites a destination. There is no artifact deletion API or automatic domain pruning.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Persistent schema eight preserves retained legacy workflow and artifact meanings. Ordinary work refuses schemas one through seven until supported maintenance migrates them. Full and Projects-only template imports do not rewrite historical captures.

reliances.statement: Validating the configured daily PDF relies on local Python with pypdf; no dedicated installed renderer contract covers that external tooling.
